subject: Model health: post-demo action items & rollback options
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@crestbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model health: post-demo action items & rollback options

Hi Daniel — great demo earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap and recommended next steps focused on model fit and guarding against regressions after version changes:

1) Observations from our run-through
   - Best fit for your transaction categorization workload in the sandbox: redwood-open-6b-int8 (lowest latency with 0.6 token/sec improvement) and rw-medium-compat-v2.0 (highest precision on our retail prompt set).
   - We shipped sample prompts and benchmark scripts in the attached eval pack.

2) Immediate recommendations
   - Run the attached eval pack (crest_eval_pack_20261010.zip) against the rw-medium-compat family and the int8 variants. The pack includes: prompt_set_crestmt_v1.xlsx, labeled test set (2k), and a quick-run notebook.
   - If you plan to move to rw-medium-compat-v2.1 in staging, enable traffic canary (5–10%) for 48 hours and an automatic rollback window if quality drops >5% on precision for high-risk intents.

3) Rollback/pinning options (what we can do now)
   - Pin to rw-medium-compat:v2.0 for the affected endpoint (fast, non-disruptive).
   - Emergency rollback to previous container with preserved KV cache (short downtime for cache warm-up).
   - Prompt-level guardrails: we can add classification checks and rejection thresholds at the API layer while you run a deeper triage.

4) Next steps
   - Can we schedule a short call this afternoon to review the diff report and agree a mitigation path? I can loop in Rishi from Sales Eng for the canary/ops details.

Attachments: crest_eval_pack_20261010.zip (eval scripts, prompt sets), prompt_set_crestmt_v1.xlsx

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@crestbank.com>

Date: 2026-10-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model health: post-demo action items & rollback options

Vivek — thanks for the quick recap. A couple of immediate points from our side after the nightly upgrade to rw-medium-compat:v2.1 in our staging cluster:

- We observed a regression in the transaction-categorization microservice: precision down ~12% on the high-value merchant set (sample attached in the internal dashboard). False positives increased for the "utilities" bucket.
- We need clarity on the delta between v2.1 and v2.0 that could cause this (tokenization changes? new preproc?). Can you share a concise diff summary and the actionable rollback steps?

We want to avoid a production rollback if possible, but if pinning to v2.0 is the fastest way to restore baseline quality we'll do it. Also looped in Prod Ops in case we need an emergency window.

—Daniel
Daniel Park | Product Manager, Fraud & Ops
Daniel.Park@crestbank.com
Cc: prodops@crestbank.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-10T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model health: post-demo action items & rollback options

Daniel — sorry to hear about the hit. I've started a quick triage and attached a concise diff report (diff_v2.1_vs_v2.0.pdf) that highlights two likely causes: a subtle change in tokenization boundary handling and a batch-norm-like inference path that slightly alters contextual attenuation on short prompts. High-level options: 

A) Fast pin (recommended for immediate relief)
   - Pin the endpoint to rw-medium-compat:v2.0 at the routing layer (no code change). This is reversible and preserves current traffic routing. Expected to restore previous precision within minutes once warm-up completes.

B) Canary + automatic rollback (recommended if you want to keep v2.1 in test)
   - Shift 5% traffic to v2.1 for 24–48h, monitor core metrics (precision on high-value merchants, false-positive rate). If delta >5% degrade, automated rollback triggers. We can deploy this from our control plane; minimal infra involvement from CrestBank.

C) Prompt-level mitigations (short term)
   - Add a classification filter post-generation to reject low-confidence labels and route to deterministic rules for the utilities bucket. This buys time for model triage.

I've attached: diff_v2.1_vs_v2.0.pdf and a short runbook we can execute (included inside crest_eval_pack_20261010.zip as well). Also added a HubSpot action: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/CREST-4871 — Rishi has created a task for the ops window.

Can we align on a decision at 16:00 PT? I'm available and will be on the call to coordinate the pin/rollback if you choose A. If you prefer a controlled canary, we can start the config immediately.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks all — confirmed for 16:00 PT. Agenda for the 30-min call:

1) Confirm quick mitigation (pin to v2.0) vs controlled canary. Decision + owner.
2) Walk through Rishi's diff highlights and the short runbook for pin/rollback.
3) If pin chosen: schedule a warm-up window and monitor plan (owner: Crest Prod Ops).
4) If canary chosen: define alarm thresholds and rollback automation steps.

Action items before call:
- Daniel / Prod Ops: share the failing sample set or a redacted extract (if possible) so Rishi can run targeted tests (you can drop to the Drive link below).
